purpose: Map the EAzami continuous-trait taxon panel to exact Japan38 Comp1061 tips without silently collapsing infraspecific concepts.

mappings.reason: Japan38 contains Cirsium japonicum var. horridum, not an exact plain-species concept; do not collapse automatically.

mappings.note: Exact Japan38 mapping exists, but the common-nine live environment gate currently has fewer than 10 source-name-matched records.

gate_design.ml: Brownian shared-path GLS using empirical Comp1061 branch lengths in substitutions/site; exact predictor-label permutation P within the fixed exact-tip subset.
gate_design.ufboot: Topology-only sensitivity on all 1000 UFBoot trees with unit branch lengths because the UFBoot Newick lines do not retain optimized branch lengths.
gate_design.multiplicity: Benjamini-Hochberg across all 63 ML branch-aware endpoint x environment rows; no row is removed before topology analysis.
gate_design.interpretation: The UFBoot layer tests topology sign stability, not absolute evolutionary rates or dated history.

claim_boundary: Cirsium japonicum is not silently equated with the Japan38 var. horridum concept.
Cirsium verutum remains excluded from the current common-nine atlas if the predeclared occurrence-depth gate is not met.
Substitutions/site and unit-branch topology sensitivity are not calendar time.
Phylogenetic sign stability does not establish selection, adaptation or causation.
